problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the hyperbolic cylinder $\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4}=1?$

feedback.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the parabolic cylinder $(y-3)^{2}=2(x+3)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our parabolic cylinder is

$$
(y-3)^{2}=2(x+3),\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:(y-3)^{2}=2(x+3)}.
$$

This is a rightward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(-3,3).$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A rightward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(-3,3)$
